pages.text:
Your Training

    selfmastery.mn.co/posts/self-mastery-course-ii-your-training-6431101



Summary of practice

1. Listen to the Critical Judgments lesson audio

2. Write about, or re-think what the Judge has to say. Notice it’s intent to help
you be happier, feel emotionally safe, stay out of trouble, or be more successful. Seeing
this half will help lessen the judgment and hate for the judge. Also notice that it’s
method is completely opposite in effect. Seeing this contradiction will help you be more
skeptical of the Judge.

3. Write third person perspective about the Judgments of the Judge. See
them from the observer perspective. The awareness of the intent of the Judge should
help lessen the judgments. As you see the helpful intent of the Judge you may notice
that it behaves more as a child emotionally. It’s a character that never grew up.



Some notes

The way we have typically looked at the judge is as an authority figure. We started
listening to it when we were young, naive, small, and powerless. Essentially we listen
with victim ears.

So our tendency is to continue to listen as a Victim, and feel powerless to it. In this
exercise you are shifting your perspective to grow up out of the Victim perspective in
your relationship with the Judge.

One of the ways that you will know you are making real progress on changing the Judge
is when you see him/her more as a hurt child afraid of failing than as an authority
figure. This requires that you drop the victim perspective in perception, and then look
beyond what the Judge says, to what motivates him/her.

Even behind the “intent” for you to do better, is a fear of getting it wrong, being bad,
getting punished, or rejected, etc.

pages.text:
Obstacles you are likely to find

    selfmastery.mn.co/posts/self-mastery-course-ii-obstacles-you-are-likely-to-find-6431102

The Judge part of the mind we do need to make assessments. Critical thinking is
valuable. However, don’t confuse “critical thinking” with “criticism.” These are two
completely different things. Critical thinking is good. Criticism, or being critical is
hurtful. Take a moment to ponder how completely different these two expressions are
and yet the language is similar.

The scary part of not believing the Judge is that it will seem like you are giving up all the
rules you learned to follow. Those rules gave you a box to live in, and in that box of
rules you learned by hypnosis that you will be safe. Giving up the rules of the Judge may
seem like you are giving up what will keep you safe, get you love, approval, and success.

The key to getting out of this false belief trap is to recognize that the Judge’s version of
happiness, success, safety, etc, is actually to stay locked in that box with him continuing
to whip you. In the judge’s limited world this is the path to success. Judging and
criticizing the victim to get you motivated might have worked when you were 10 years
old, but it doesn’t work today.

The other thing to recognize is that you don’t have to give up all the things you want like
success, happiness, love, etc. You can have all that. You just don’t want the punishment
and berating from the Judge that causes the misery.

You also don’t need your emotions dependent on having that list of things.

Are you really giving up on your goals? I hope not, but the characters will turn it into
that. What I'm really asking you to do is to consider that the Judge berating you actually
doesn't help you get there. He/she is more demotivating than motivating.

pages.text:
Common Questions

   selfmastery.mn.co/posts/self-mastery-course-ii-common-questions-6431103

How do I get the Judge to stop?

This exercise isn’t about getting the Judge to stop. That is trying to leap too far. Besides,
repression and suppression is not a good long term strategy. We are going to work
through dismantling the Judge and judgment stories in steps. This step is about
lessening the judgments about the Judge.

First step was to perceive it's intention as trying to help. This step is about removing
judgments about the Judge. These top layerers need to come off first.

Start with shifting your story about the Judge to more of an acceptance attitude. Or see
it as a child stuck in a repetition of thoughts. Or see it as a part of your mind that has
been hypnotized into just seeing the same things over and over again and needs help
getting free from it’s limited approach, but doesn’t even know that.

From there you can go to the next step of letting go.
